# MOVING DAY ESSENTIALS — ONE-PAGE PRINTABLE

**Keep this list and everything on it IN THE CAR, not on the truck.**

---

## 🔑 DOCUMENTS & MONEY
- [ ] Driver's licenses and passports
- [ ] Vehicle titles, registrations, insurance cards
- [ ] Moving contract, Bill of Lading, inventory sheet
- [ ] Lease or closing docs (both homes)
- [ ] Vehicle shipping receipt and carrier contact info
- [ ] Wallets, credit/debit cards
- [ ] Cash ($200–$300 small bills for tips, tolls, emergencies)
- [ ] Phones and chargers (car + wall)
- [ ] Phone power bank (fully charged)

---

## 💊 HEALTH & MEDS
- [ ] All current prescriptions (both people)
- [ ] Basic first-aid kit (bandages, ibuprofen, antacids, allergy meds)
- [ ] Hand sanitizer, wet wipes, tissues
- [ ] Health insurance cards
- [ ] Glasses, contacts, solution (if applicable)
- [ ] Sunscreen

---

## 🐕 DOG KIT
- [ ] Leash, harness, collar with current ID tag
- [ ] Vaccination records and rabies certificate
- [ ] Microchip number written down
- [ ] 5+ days of food in a sealed container
- [ ] Collapsible water bowl and water bottle
- [ ] Treats and favorite toy
- [ ] Blanket or bed that smells like home
- [ ] Poop bags (full roll)
- [ ] Any medications or calming aids
- [ ] Crate or car barrier/seatbelt harness
- [ ] Paper towels and an old towel (car sickness backup)
- [ ] Photo of your dog on your phone (in case of separation)

---

## 👕 OVERNIGHT BAG (× 2 PEOPLE)
- [ ] 3 days of clothes (layers — you'll cross climates)
- [ ] Pajamas
- [ ] Toiletries (toothbrush, toothpaste, deodorant, shampoo, soap)
- [ ] Towels (1 each — your packed ones may arrive late)
- [ ] Rain jacket or light hoodie
- [ ] Comfortable driving shoes and walking shoes

---

## 🍎 FOOD & DRINK
- [ ] Cooler with ice
- [ ] Water bottles (people and dog)
- [ ] Road snacks (protein bars, fruit, nuts, crackers)
- [ ] Reusable bags for gas station stops
- [ ] Paper towels and napkins

---

## 🔧 TOOLS & CAR
- [ ] Flashlight (with extra batteries)
- [ ] Multi-tool or basic screwdriver set
- [ ] Duct tape and zip ties
- [ ] Box cutter or utility knife
- [ ] Tape and a marker (for relabeling)
- [ ] Jumper cables
- [ ] Tire pressure gauge
- [ ] Spare tire, jack, and lug wrench (confirm they're in the car)
- [ ] Windshield scraper (mountain passes)
- [ ] Blanket for roadside emergencies
- [ ] Umbrella

---

## 🏠 HANDOFF & LOCKUP
- [ ] Keys to old home — return after walk-through
- [ ] Garage door remotes
- [ ] Mailbox keys
- [ ] Gate codes / building fob
- [ ] Keys or access codes to new home
- [ ] Landlord and property manager phone numbers (old and new)
- [ ] Final walk-through photos taken ✓
- [ ] Final meter readings photographed ✓

---

## ✅ BEFORE YOU PULL AWAY
- [ ] Every room checked — closets, cabinets, attic, garage, behind doors
- [ ] Fridge and freezer emptied and cleaned
- [ ] All windows locked, thermostat set or off
- [ ] Water off (if required)
- [ ] Trash out
- [ ] Mover has your phone number and Oregon address
- [ ] Mover tip paid (if tipping: $20–$50 per crew member is common for a full day)
- [ ] Goodbye photo of the place if you want one 📸

---

*Print this page. Tape it to the dashboard or keep it on a clipboard. Check off items as you load the car the night before.*

---
---

# 6–8 WEEK CALENDAR OF REMINDERS

Below is a week-by-week schedule you can drop into Google Calendar, Apple Reminders, or any app. Each item is written as a standalone reminder with a suggested day. Adjust the actual dates to your move date and set alerts for 9 AM so you have the full day to act.

**How to use:** Count back from your move date. If your move date is a Saturday, Week 1 Monday is the Monday of that week. Week 8 Monday is 8 Mondays before that.

---

## WEEK 8 (8 weeks before move day)

**Monday**
- Get 3–4 moving company quotes OR reserve a rental truck/container. Verify USDOT numbers.

**Tuesday**
- Check lease notice requirement. Draft and send written notice to landlord today if 60-day notice is required.

**Wednesday**
- Research Oregon rental listings and neighborhoods. Set up search alerts on Zillow, Apartments.com, Craigslist.

**Thursday**
- Schedule vet visit for the dog: health check, vaccine records, rabies certificate copy.

**Friday**
- Start the Documents Folder: gather IDs, titles, insurance cards, lease, tax records. Put them in one place.

---

## WEEK 7

**Monday**
- Compare mover quotes and vehicle shipping quotes. Make a decision this week.

**Tuesday**
- Book the mover or truck. Read the contract and confirm valuation coverage.

**Wednesday**
- If shipping a vehicle: book the carrier. Confirm open vs. enclosed and pickup window.

**Thursday**
- Book temporary housing in Oregon (dog-friendly Airbnb or extended-stay) if your new place won't be ready on arrival.

**Friday**
- Call Oregon utility providers: electric, gas, water, trash. Ask about lead times. Schedule internet installation NOW.

---

## WEEK 6

**Monday**
- Begin the Great Declutter. Start with the garage, storage unit, and junk drawers. Decide: keep, sell, donate, trash.

**Tuesday**
- List sellable items on Facebook Marketplace, Craigslist, or Nextdoor. Price to move fast.

**Wednesday**
- Order packing supplies: boxes (small, medium, large, wardrobe), packing tape, bubble wrap, markers, paper.

**Thursday**
- Notify your employer and partner's employer of the move date. Ask about remote work, relocation assistance, and payroll address changes.

**Friday**
- Sign the Oregon lease or confirm closing date. Save a copy of the lease or contract to your Move folder.

---

## WEEK 5

**Monday**
- Pack Room 1: Guest bedroom, storage room, or least-used space. Label every box with room name and contents.

**Tuesday**
- Pack Room 2: Office, books, decor, wall art. Wrap frames in towels.

**Wednesday**
- Schedule donation pickups (Habitat ReStore, Goodwill, Salvation Army) for next week.

**Thursday**
- Send landlord formal written move-out notice if you haven't yet (30-day deadline). Request a move-out inspection.

**Friday**
- Notify banks, credit cards, and insurance companies of your upcoming address change. Set the effective date for move day.

---

## WEEK 4

**Monday**
- File change of address with USPS at usps.com. Set the start date for ~2 days before your move.

**Tuesday**
- Schedule Ohio utility shutoffs (electric, gas, water, trash, cable/internet) for the day after you leave.

**Wednesday**
- Confirm Oregon utility start dates. Confirm internet install appointment.

**Thursday**
- Pack Room 3: Kitchen — non-essentials (specialty appliances, baking supplies, extra dishes, cookbooks). Keep one pot, one pan, basic utensils, and plates for two until the last day.

**Friday**
- Cancel or transfer subscriptions and memberships: gym, CSA box, newspaper, streaming services tied to location, library cards. See if anything has an early termination fee.

---

## WEEK 3

**Monday**
- Pack Room 4: Living room — books, games, decor, media, seasonal items. Leave the couch, one lamp, and a screen for the last week.

**Tuesday**
- Pack Room 5: Bathroom — extras (towels, cleaning supplies, backup toiletries). Keep one set of towels and daily toiletries out.

**Wednesday**
- Confirm mover: arrival time, crew size, payment method, final estimate in writing. OR confirm truck/container pickup time.

**Thursday**
- Car maintenance check: oil, tires, brakes, battery, fluids, wipers. Top off or schedule service.

**Friday**
- Research Oregon DMV requirements: documents needed for license, vehicle registration, emissions test (if Portland metro). Write a checklist and put it in the Move folder.

---

## WEEK 2

**Monday**
- Pack Room 6: Master bedroom — off-season clothes, extra bedding, nightstand items. Leave sheets, pillows, and 3 days of clothes.

**Tuesday**
- Finish selling or donating remaining declutter items. Put unsold items at the curb or schedule bulk trash pickup.

**Wednesday**
- Pack the dog travel kit: leash, harness, food (5+ days), bowls, meds, records, blanket, toy, poop bags, paper towels. Keep it accessible.

**Thursday**
- Get a new ID tag for the dog with your phone number. Confirm all overnight lodging along the route is booked and dog-friendly.

**Friday**
- Do a dress rehearsal: lay out the Moving Day Essentials list and check every item. Charge the power bank. Load the cooler and snacks the night before.

---

## WEEK 1

**Monday**
- Pack the last of everything except what you'll use today through move day. Label boxes clearly.

**Tuesday**
- Defrost and clean the fridge and freezer. Donate or eat all perishable food.

**Wednesday**
- Take photos of all valuables, serial numbers, and the condition of your current home (every room, closets, floors, walls).

**Thursday (day before move)**
- Finish packing. Set aside the overnight bags and dog kit. Confirm the mover's arrival time or pick up the truck. Load the car with essentials tonight.

**Friday (MOVE DAY — adjust to your actual day)**
- Walk-through every room, closet, cabinet, attic, garage.
- Photograph utility meters.
- Meet movers, review inventory, sign Bill of Lading.
- Hand over keys, remotes, fobs. Get a receipt.
- Load the dog last. Hit the road.

---

## WEEK +1 (first week in Oregon)

**Monday**
- Photograph the new place at move-in. Document any existing damage and send it to the landlord in writing.

**Tuesday**
- Confirm all utilities are on and working. Test internet. Locate breaker box, water shutoff, gas shutoff.

**Wednesday**
- Schedule Oregon DMV visit: bring proof of identity, proof of residency, vehicle title, insurance, and payment. Get your license and start the registration process.

**Thursday**
- Take the dog to the new Oregon vet. Transfer records. Ask about the county dog license.

**Friday**
- Update microchip registry, voter registration, remaining subscriptions, and anything you missed. Breathe. You made it.

---

## QUICK-IMPORT FORMAT

If you use **Google Calendar**, create a new calendar called "Move" and add each item above as an all-day event with a 9:00 AM notification. Color-code by category (housing = blue, packing = green, dog = orange, admin = yellow).

If you use **Apple Reminders**, create a list called "Move Checklist" and set each item with a date and a morning alert.

If you use **Todoist, Notion, or Trello**, paste each week as a section or column and assign items to M, P, or J.

---

turns.text:
# ROOM-BY-ROOM PACKING & DECLUTTER CHECKLIST

---

## SYSTEM OVERVIEW (Use this for every room)

### Declutter Decision Flow

For every item, ask these four questions in order:

```
1. Have I used this in the last 12 months?
   → NO → Go to 2
   → YES → KEEP (unless it's cheap to replace and expensive to move)

2. Would I buy this again at full price?
   → NO → Go to 3
   → YES → KEEP

3. Is it worth more than $25 and in good condition?
   → YES → SELL (Facebook Marketplace, Craigslist, garage sale)
   → NO → Go to 4

4. Is it functional and clean?
   → YES → DONATE (Goodwill, Habitat ReStore, Buy Nothing group)
   → NO → TRASH / RECYCLE
```

**Rule of thumb:** If moving it costs more than replacing it, let it go. A $40 bookshelf that takes up truck space and weighs 60 lbs is not worth moving 2,400 miles.

---

### Labeling System

Write all three lines on **two sides** of every box in thick marker:

```
Line 1: ROOM NAME (e.g., KITCHEN)
Line 2: Contents summary (e.g., plates, bowls, mugs)
Line 3: Priority tag
```

**Priority tags:**
- **🔴 OPEN FIRST** — You need this within hours of arrival (sheets, towels, toilet paper, coffee maker, dog bowls)
- **🟡 OPEN SOON** — Need within 2–3 days (most clothes, basic cookware, office setup)
- **🟢 OPEN LATER** — Can wait a week or more (decor, books, seasonal, storage)
- **⚠️ FRAGILE** — Add this on top of any priority tag. Also write FRAGILE on the top and all four sides. Draw arrows pointing up.

**Color-coded tape (optional but powerful):** Assign a tape color to each room. When the movers or you unload, boxes go straight to the right room without reading labels.

| Room | Tape Color |
|---|---|
| Kitchen | Red |
| Master Bedroom | Blue |
| Living Room | Green |
| Office | Yellow |
| Bathroom | White |
| Garage / Storage | Orange |

---

### Fragile Packing Tips (Reference for Every Room)

- **Plates:** Stand on edge vertically in small boxes, never flat-stacked. Wrap each plate in packing paper or a dish towel. Place crumpled paper between them.
- **Glasses and mugs:** Stuff the inside with paper, wrap the outside, place upside down in a box with dividers or a cell kit. Small boxes only.
- **Mirrors and frames:** Make an X with painter's tape across the glass (limits shatter spread). Wrap in bubble wrap, stand on edge in a box, never lay flat.
- **Electronics:** Use original boxes if you kept them. If not, wrap in bubble wrap, fill gaps with towels or packing paper. Photograph cable setups before disconnecting.
- **Lamps:** Remove shades and bulbs. Wrap the base in bubble wrap. Pack shades in separate boxes nested inside each other with paper between them.
- **Knives:** Wrap each blade in cardboard or several layers of paper. Tape the cardboard closed. Bundle them together and label SHARP.
- **Liquids:** Place in a zip-lock bag first, then pack upright. Tighten all lids. Consider tossing anything half-empty and cheap to replace.
- **General rule:** If you can hear items shifting when you gently shake the box, add more packing material. No rattling, no breaking.

---

## ROOM 1: KITCHEN

**Your inventory notes:** Lots of dishes, 3 small appliances, spice rack.

### Estimated Effort
| Metric | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Total boxes | 12–18 (mostly small and medium) |
| Suggested box mix | 8 small, 6 medium, 2 large, 1 dish-barrel if you have one |
| Time to declutter | 2–3 hours |
| Time to pack | 4–6 hours (the kitchen is always the longest room) |
| Recommended schedule | Declutter in Week 6. Pack non-essentials in Week 4. Pack the rest the day before. |

### Declutter First

| Category | Keep | Sell / Donate | Trash |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dishes and plates | One full set for your household size + a few extras | Duplicate sets, chipped pieces, novelty mugs you never use | Cracked, stained, or broken items |
| Glasses and mugs | Daily-use glasses + a few wine/beer glasses | Promotional cups, mismatched sets, excess travel mugs | Anything chipped |
| Cookware | 1 large pot, 1 small pot, 1 skillet, 1 baking sheet, 1 casserole dish | Duplicate pans, warped baking sheets, specialty items you used once | Scratched nonstick with flaking coating |
| Utensils and tools | 1 set of cooking utensils, 1 good knife set, can opener, peeler, spatula, tongs | Duplicate whisks, rusty tools, single-use gadgets (avocado slicer, banana cutter) | Broken or rusty items |
| Small appliances (3) | Keep the ones you use weekly | Sell or donate anything you haven't used in 6 months | Broken or missing parts |
| Spice rack | Keep spices less than 1 year old | — | Expired spices (smell test: if it smells like nothing, toss it) |
| Food and pantry | Sealed, non-perishable items you'll actually eat | Donate unopened canned goods and dry goods to a food bank | Expired food, open packages you won't finish |
| Cleaning supplies | 1 all-purpose cleaner, dish soap, sponge for move-out cleaning | — | Nearly empty bottles, duplicate products (cheaper to buy new in Oregon) |
| Tupperware and food storage | Matching sets with lids only | Lidless containers, excess takeout containers | Stained, warped, or melted items |

### Packing Order

**Pack in Week 4 (non-essentials):**
- [ ] Baking supplies and specialty bakeware
- [ ] Extra dish sets and serving platters
- [ ] Cookbooks
- [ ] Small appliances you won't use in the next 2 weeks (decide which one or two you keep out)
- [ ] Vases, decorative kitchen items
- [ ] Wine glasses and bar tools
- [ ] Spice rack (bag each jar in a zip-lock in case of leaks, pack upright in a small box)

**Pack in Week 2 (scaling down):**
- [ ] All remaining dishes except 2 plates, 2 bowls, 2 mugs, 2 glasses
- [ ] All pots and pans except 1 pot and 1 skillet
- [ ] All utensils except 2 forks, 2 knives, 2 spoons, 1 spatula, 1 cooking spoon
- [ ] Remaining small appliances except the coffee maker (or whatever you can't live without)
- [ ] Remaining pantry items (sealed, non-perishable)

**Pack last (day before or morning of move):**
- [ ] Coffee maker and daily mugs
- [ ] Last 2 plates, 2 bowls, 2 glasses
- [ ] Last pot, skillet, and utensils
- [ ] Dish soap, sponge, paper towels (keep paper towels for the car)
- [ ] Trash bags (keep a few for the car and for move-in)
- [ ] Cooler (load it with road snacks and drinks last)

### Kitchen Packing Tips
- **Heaviest items in small boxes.** Plates, cast iron, canned goods — small box, always.
- **Wrap every dish individually.** Use packing paper, newspaper (ink can transfer to white dishes), or dish towels and t-shirts as free padding.
- **Stand plates vertically** like records in a crate, not stacked flat.
- **Nesting:** Put small bowls inside large bowls with paper between them.
- **Knives:** Cardboard sleeve taped shut for each knife, or wrap the whole block.
- **Appliances:** Remove glass carafes and blades. Pack them separately and label them.
- **Under the sink:** Tighten every cap. Put each bottle in a zip-lock bag. Pack upright in a bin or small box lined with a trash bag.
- **Spice jars:** Rubber-band the lids, bag each jar, pack upright in a small box. Consider tossing and rebuying — spices are light but fragile and leak easily.

### Box Labels for This Room
```
KITCHEN — Plates, bowls (fragile) — 🔴 OPEN FIRST ⚠️ FRAGILE
KITCHEN — Pots, pans, baking — 🟡 OPEN SOON
KITCHEN — Coffee maker, mugs, utensils — 🔴 OPEN FIRST
KITCHEN — Spices, pantry dry goods — 🟡 OPEN SOON
KITCHEN — Bakeware, serving, cookbooks — 🟢 OPEN LATER
KITCHEN — Small appliances — 🟡 OPEN SOON
KITCHEN — Under-sink, cleaning supplies — 🟢 OPEN LATER
```

---

## ROOM 2: MASTER BEDROOM

### Estimated Effort
| Metric | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Total boxes | 8–12 |
| Suggested box mix | 2 small, 4 medium, 2 large, 2 wardrobe |
| Time to declutter | 1.5–2 hours |
| Time to pack | 2–3 hours |
| Recommended schedule | Declutter in Week 6. Pack non-essentials in Week 3. Pack the rest the morning of. |

### Declutter First

| Category | Keep | Sell / Donate | Trash |
|---|---|---|---|
| Clothing (your side) | Clothes you've worn in the last year, fits well, in good condition | Anything that doesn't fit, you haven't worn in a year, or makes you feel nothing | Stained, torn, worn-out items |
| Shoes | Daily pairs + 1 dress, 1 seasonal | Duplicates, uncomfortable pairs, worn-out soles | Broken or unwearable |
| Bedding | 2 sheet sets, 2 pillow sets, 1 comforter, 1 extra blanket | Excess flat sheets, old pillows (replace every 2 years), duplicate comforters | Stained, torn, or flat pillows |
| Nightstand items | Daily items, charger, book | — | Old receipts, dead batteries, broken items |
| Jewelry and accessories | Worn regularly or sentimental | Sell valuable pieces you don't wear | Broken costume jewelry |
| Under-bed storage | Evaluate each item using the decision flow | — | — |

### Packing Order

**Pack in Week 3:**
- [ ] Off-season clothing (winter coats if moving in summer, etc.) — use wardrobe boxes for hanging clothes
- [ ] Extra bedding and pillows (vacuum-seal bags save huge space)
- [ ] Books and decor from nightstands and dressers
- [ ] Under-bed storage items
- [ ] Wall art and mirrors (tape glass, wrap, stand on edge)
- [ ] Jewelry box (carry this in the car, not on the truck)

**Pack in Week 2:**
- [ ] Most remaining clothes, leaving 3 days of outfits and sleepwear
- [ ] Extra shoes
- [ ] Dresser drawers: you can leave soft clothes in dresser drawers if the movers allow it — wrap the dresser in stretch wrap to keep drawers shut

**Pack last (morning of move day):**
- [ ] Sheets and pillows (strip the bed, stuff them in a trash bag, label it, toss it in the car or on top of the truck load)
- [ ] Phone chargers and bedside items
- [ ] Last 3 days of clothes (already in your overnight bag)
- [ ] Hamper with dirty laundry (tie the bag shut, it goes on the truck — no need to wash first)

### Box Labels for This Room
```
MASTER BED — Sheets, pillows, blankets — 🔴 OPEN FIRST
MASTER BED — Hanging clothes (wardrobe box 1 of 2) — 🟡 OPEN SOON
MASTER BED — Off-season clothes — 🟢 OPEN LATER
MASTER BED — Shoes, accessories — 🟡 OPEN SOON
MASTER BED — Nightstand, books, decor — 🟢 OPEN LATER
MASTER BED — Wall art (fragile) — 🟢 OPEN LATER ⚠️ FRAGILE
```

---

## ROOM 3: PARTNER'S CLOSET

### Estimated Effort
| Metric | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Total boxes | 4–8 |
| Suggested box mix | 2 medium, 2 large, 2 wardrobe |
| Time to declutter | 1.5–2 hours |
| Time to pack | 1.5–2 hours |
| Recommended schedule | Declutter in Week 6. Pack in Week 3. Leave 3 days of clothes out. |

### Declutter First

Use the same clothing decision flow as the master bedroom. Partner owns this process — schedule a 2-hour block, put on music, and make it a focused session.

**Extra closet-specific tips:**
- Try the "hanger trick": turn all hangers backward now. After 2 weeks, anything still backward hasn't been worn — strong candidate for donate or sell.
- Shoes: if you haven't worn them in a year and they're not formal/special occasion, let them go.
- Bags and purses: keep 1 daily, 1 travel, 1 dress. Donate the rest.
- Hats, scarves, belts: keep what you wear. Donate the rest.

### Packing Order

**Pack in Week 3:**
- [ ] Off-season clothes into wardrobe boxes or large boxes
- [ ] Shoes in medium boxes (stuff shoes with socks or paper to keep shape)
- [ ] Bags, accessories, hats
- [ ] Anything from the top shelf or floor of the closet

**Pack last:**
- [ ] 3 days of outfits and sleepwear → overnight bag in the car
- [ ] Hangers: bundle in groups of 10 with a rubber band or tie, or leave on clothes in wardrobe boxes

### Box Labels for This Room
```
PARTNER CLOSET — Hanging clothes (wardrobe box) — 🟡 OPEN SOON
PARTNER CLOSET — Shoes, bags, accessories — 🟡 OPEN SOON
PARTNER CLOSET — Off-season, shelf items — 🟢 OPEN LATER
```

---

## ROOM 4: LIVING ROOM

### Estimated Effort
| Metric | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Total boxes | 6–10 |
| Suggested box mix | 2 small, 4 medium, 2 large |
| Time to declutter | 1–2 hours |
| Time to pack | 2–3 hours (more if many books or media) |
| Recommended schedule | Declutter in Week 5. Pack non-essentials in Week 3. Leave one lamp and the couch until move day. |

### Declutter First

| Category | Keep | Sell / Donate | Trash |
|---|---|---|---|
| Books | Favorites, reference, unread books you'll actually read | Books you've read and won't reread, outdated guides | Damaged, moldy, water-stained |
| Media (DVDs, games, CDs) | Only if you still use physical media | Sell or donate the rest — most content is streaming now | Broken cases, scratched discs |
| Decor | Items you love and will display in the new home | Trend pieces you're tired of, impulse buys | Broken or damaged items

# ROOM-BY-ROOM PACKING (CONTINUED)

## Running Box Inventory Tracker

Before we dive in, here's where you stand. I'll update this after each room.

| Box Size | On Hand | Used So Far (Rooms 1–4) | Remaining | Needed for Rooms 5–9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Small (30) | 30 | 12 (Kitchen 8, Bedroom 2, Living 2) | 18 | ~14–20 |
| Medium (20) | 20 | 16 (Kitchen 6, Bedroom 4, Closet 2, Living 4) | 4 | ~12–18 |
| Large (8) | 8 | 8 (Kitchen 2, Bedroom 2, Closet 2, Living 2) | 0 | ~10–16 |
| Wardrobe (4) | 4 | 4 (Bedroom 2, Closet 2) | 0 | 0–2 |

**Bottom line:** You're short on medium and large boxes and nearly out. Order or scavenge **15–20 medium and 12–18 large boxes** before you start these next rooms. Wardrobe boxes are probably covered unless Partner has a lot more hanging clothes. Small boxes are okay but could run tight if the garage is heavy — get 5–10 more to be safe.

**Free box sources:** Liquor stores (sturdy, divided — great for glasses), grocery stores (banana boxes are tough), Nextdoor / Buy Nothing groups, U-Haul box exchange, bookstores.

---

## ROOM 5: HOME OFFICE

### Estimated Effort
| Metric | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Total boxes | 6–10 |
| Suggested box mix | 4–6 small, 3–4 medium, 1 large (for monitor or printer) |
| Time to declutter | 2–3 hours (paper shredding takes the longest) |
| Time to pack | 2–3 hours |
| Recommended schedule | Declutter in Week 5. Pack non-essentials in Week 3. Pack the desk setup on the last working day before the move. |

### Declutter First

| Category | Keep | Sell / Donate | Trash / Shred |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper files | Last 3 years of tax returns, legal docs, medical records, warranty docs for items you're keeping | Old manuals for items you no longer own | Shred: bank statements older than 1 year, old pay stubs, pre-approved credit offers, outdated insurance docs |
| Books and reference | Professional references you actually use | Outdated editions, textbooks from 10 years ago | Water-damaged, moldy |
| Office supplies | 1 pack of pens, 1 tape dispenser, scissors, stapler, notepad, paper clips | Excess supplies (donate to a school or church) | Dried-out markers, broken pens, stiff rubber bands |
| Cables and tech | Cables for devices you currently own, 1 universal charging cable, 1 power strip, 1 extension cord | Old phone chargers, mystery cables (if you don't know what it's for, you don't need it) | Frayed or damaged cables |
| Furniture | Desk and chair if worth moving | Cheap particle-board furniture that won't survive the trip | Broken, wobbly items |

**Paper rule of thumb:** If you can access it digitally (bank statements, bills, insurance EOBs), shred the paper copy. Scan anything you're unsure about before shredding — use your phone camera or a free scanning app like Adobe Scan.

### Packing Order

**Pack in Week 3:**
- [ ] Books and reference materials — small boxes only (books are heavy)
- [ ] Filing cabinet contents — keep the folders intact, pack them upright in a medium box like they're in a drawer
- [ ] Art, diplomas, framed items from office walls — tape glass, bubble wrap, stand on edge
- [ ] Printer (remove ink cartridges, bag them separately, pack the printer in original box or wrap in bubble wrap in a medium box)
- [ ] Extra office supplies
- [ ] Shred and recycle the discard pile

**Pack in Week 2:**
- [ ] Non-essential cables and peripherals (extra keyboard, speakers, webcam if not needed for work)
- [ ] Desk accessories and organizers
- [ ] Remaining books and binders

**Pack last (last working day or morning of move):**
- [ ] Computer / laptop and power cable → carry in the car, never on the truck
- [ ] Monitor — wrap in a towel, place in original box or between two pieces of cardboard taped together, then in a large box padded on all sides. If you have the original foam inserts, use them. Mark FRAGILE on every side.
- [ ] Mouse, keyboard, headset, and daily-use cables
- [ ] Modem and router (you may need internet until the last day — pack these after your last email check)
- [ ] External hard drive or backup drive → car, not the truck
- [ ] Any work files or documents you need access to during the drive

### Fragile Packing Tips — Office Specific
- **Monitor:** This is the most fragile item in the office. Original box is best. If you don't have it, make a cardboard sandwich: cut two pieces of cardboard larger than the screen, place the wrapped monitor between them, tape the cardboard together, then place the whole assembly in a large box with 3+ inches of padding on every side. Never lay a monitor face down.
- **Hard drives:** Wrap in bubble wrap and pack in a small box with padding. Better yet, carry them in a padded bag in the car. Temperature extremes and vibration can damage drives.
- **Printer:** Remove ink/toner cartridges and bag them in zip-locks (they leak). Tape the scanner lid shut. Wrap the printer in bubble wrap.
- **Cables:** Coil each cable individually and secure with a twist tie or velcro strap. Put all cables in one labeled zip-lock bag or small box. Photograph your desk cable setup before disconnecting.

### Box Labels for This Room

OFFICE — Computer, monitor, keyboard (fragile) — 🔴 OPEN FIRST ⚠️ FRAGILE
OFFICE — Modem, router, cables — 🔴 OPEN FIRST
OFFICE — Files, tax docs, legal papers — 🟡 OPEN SOON
OFFICE — Books, references — 🟢 OPEN LATER
OFFICE — Printer, ink, office supplies — 🟡 OPEN SOON
OFFICE — Desk art, diplomas (fragile) — 🟢 OPEN LATER ⚠️ FRAGILE
```

## ROOM 6: BATHROOMS

*Covering all bathrooms as one section — scale up if you have more than two.*

### Estimated Effort
| Metric | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Total boxes | 3–5 |
| Suggested box mix | 2–3 small, 1–2 medium |
| Time to declutter | 1–1.5 hours |
| Time to pack | 1–1.5 hours |
| Recommended schedule | Declutter in Week 4. Pack non-essentials in Week 3. Pack the daily kit the morning of move day. |

### Declutter First

| Category | Keep | Sell / Donate | Trash |
|---|---|---|---|
| Medications | Current prescriptions, unexpired OTC meds you use | — | Expired meds (take to a pharmacy drop-off, don't flush) |
| Toiletries | Products you use daily and are more than ¼ full | Unopened, unused products (donate to a shelter) | Nearly empty bottles, dried-out products, expired sunscreen |
| Towels | 2 bath towels per person + 2 hand towels + 2 washcloths | Excess towels (animal shelters always need towels) | Stained, threadbare, musty towels |
| Hair tools | Dryer, iron, or styling tools you use regularly | Duplicates, old tools | Frayed cords, broken tools |
| Cleaning supplies | 1 bathroom cleaner, 1 toilet cleaner (for move-out cleaning) | — | Nearly empty bottles (cheaper to rebuy than to pack and risk leaks across 2,400 miles) |
| First aid | Restock a basic kit: bandages, antibiotic ointment, ibuprofen, Benadryl, tweezers, thermometer | — | Expired items, dried-out ointments |
| Makeup and skincare | Daily-use products only | Unopened extras (donate or give away) | Expired makeup (mascara > 3 months, foundation > 1 year, lipstick > 2 years) |

**Bathroom declutter mantra:** This room has the highest percentage of expired, nearly empty, or replaceable items. Be ruthless. You can buy shampoo in Oregon.

### Packing Order

**Pack in Week 3:**
- [ ] Guest bathroom entirely (if you have one) — towels, decor, under-sink extras
- [ ] Extra towels and linens from the main bathroom
- [ ] Backup toiletries, bulk products
- [ ] Bathroom decor (shower curtain can stay up until the last day)
- [ ] Hair tools you don't use daily
- [ ] Medicine cabinet extras (keep daily meds out)

**Pack in Week 2:**
- [ ] Under-sink supplies (tighten all lids, zip-lock each bottle, pack upright)
- [ ] Excess cleaning products — consider tossing rather than risking leaks
- [ ] Scale, wastebasket, bath mat (if you're done with them)

**Pack last (morning of move day):**
- [ ] Toothbrushes, toothpaste, deodorant, face wash, razor → into your overnight toiletry bag in the car
- [ ] Daily medications → into a labeled zip-lock in the car, never on the truck
- [ ] Last-use towels (1 per person) → stuff into a trash bag, label it, toss on top of the truck load or in the car
- [ ] Shower curtain and rings (pull it down last)
- [ ] Toilet paper — keep one roll for the drive and one for the first night at the new place. Put them in the car. This is not a joke. You will thank yourself.
- [ ] Plunger and toilet brush — clean them, bag them, they go on the truck

### Fragile Packing Tips — Bathroom Specific
- **Mirrors:** Tape an X across the glass, wrap in bubble wrap, pack vertically.
- **Perfume and cologne:** Wrap each bottle in bubble wrap, place in a zip-lock bag (glass + liquid = leak risk), pack upright in a small box padded on all sides. Or carry your favorites in the car.
- **Liquids general rule:** Every lid gets tightened, every bottle goes in a zip-lock, every box with liquids gets a trash bag liner at the bottom. Pack liquids standing up.

### Box Labels for This Room
```
BATHROOM — Daily towels, shower curtain, bath mat — 🔴 OPEN FIRST
BATHROOM — Under-sink supplies, cleaning (liquids upright) — 🟡 OPEN SOON
BATHROOM — Guest bath, extras, decor — 🟢 OPEN LATER
BATHROOM — Medicine, first aid (keep accessible) — 🔴 OPEN FIRST
```

## ROOM 7: GARAGE

**Your inventory notes:** Tools, lawn mower, 2 bikes, storage bins.

### Estimated Effort
| Metric | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Total boxes | 6–10 (plus loose large items) |
| Suggested box mix | 4–6 small (hardware is heavy), 3–4 medium, 2–3 large |
| Non-boxed items | Lawn mower, 2 bikes, workbench (maybe), shelving |
| Time to declutter | 3–4 hours (garages accumulate years of stuff) |
| Time to pack | 3–4 hours |
| Recommended schedule | Declutter in Week 6. Pack in Weeks 4–3. Drain fuel and prep large items in Week 2. |

### Declutter First

| Category | Keep | Sell / Donate | Trash |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hand tools | Quality tools you actually use: hammer, screwdrivers, pliers, wrenches, tape measure, level, drill | Duplicate or cheap tools, tools for projects you'll never do | Rusted, broken, dull beyond sharpening |
| Power tools | Drill, circular saw, or others you use regularly | Sell specialty tools you used once (Craigslist, Facebook) | Non-functional, missing parts |
| Lawn mower | **Decision point:** Will you have a yard in Oregon? If yes, is it cheaper to move or replace? A basic push mower costs $150–$300 new but takes significant truck space. | Sell if you're moving to an apartment or won't have a yard | — |
| Bikes (2) | Keep if you'll ride them in Oregon | Sell if they're unused or low-value | Rusted, flat-tired, not worth repairing |
| Storage bins | Open every bin and apply the decision flow to the contents. Keep the bins themselves only if they're in good shape. | Donate contents you don't need | Cracked or lidless bins |
| Hardware and fasteners | Consolidate into one small organizer: screws, nails, anchors, picture hangers, zip ties | Excess or project-specific hardware | Rusty, mixed junk drawers of mystery parts |
| Automotive supplies | Jumper cables, tire gauge, emergency kit, motor oil (1 qt for the drive) | Excess or old oil, coolant, brake fluid — take to an auto parts store for recycling, never trash | Dried-out rags, old wiper blades |
| Seasonal and holiday | Genuinely used decorations and items | Excess or duplicate holiday decorations | Broken lights, dried-out items, things you forgot you had |
| Paint and chemicals | **Do not move these on a truck.** Most movers won't take paint, solvents, propane tanks, gasoline, or aerosols. | Donate usable paint to Habitat ReStore | Dry out old paint cans and trash them per local rules. Take chemicals to a hazardous waste drop-off. |
| Gardening | Quality tools: shovel, rake, pruners, hose | Excess pots (heavy and cheap to replace), old soil bags | Broken or rusted tools |

### Lawn Mower Decision
- **If keeping:** Drain all fuel and oil before moving. Movers and truck rental companies do not allow fuel in transit. Run it dry or siphon the tank. Disconnect the spark plug. Clean the deck. Wrap the blade in cardboard. It goes loose on the truck, not in a box.
- **If selling:** List it 3–4 weeks before the move. Price it to sell fast — $50–$100 for a used push mower moves quickly.

### Bike Prep
- Remove pedals and turn handlebars sideways to reduce the footprint.
- If you have bike boxes (from a bike shop — ask, they usually give them away), use those.
- If not, wrap the frames in moving blankets or bubble wrap and secure with stretch wrap.
- Deflate tires slightly for altitude changes on mountain passes.
- Bikes go on the truck last (loaded first to come off first) or on a car-mounted bike rack.

### Packing Order

**Pack in Week 4:**
- [ ] Storage bins — open each one, declutter, repack keepers, label the bin with the new room destination
- [ ] Seasonal and holiday items
- [ ] Gardening tools and supplies
- [ ] Excess hardware and shop supplies

**Pack in Week 3:**
- [ ] Hand tools — wrap sharp edges in cardboard or towels, pack heavy tools in small boxes
- [ ] Power tools — remove batteries, wrap cords, use original cases if available, otherwise bubble wrap in medium boxes
- [ ] Remaining garage shelving contents

**Pack in Week 2:**
- [ ] Drain lawn mower fuel and oil. Clean and prep.
- [ ] Prep bikes (pedals off, handlebars turned, tires deflated)
- [ ] Dispose of paint, chemicals, propane tanks, old oil at hazardous waste drop-off
- [ ] Break down shelving if you're taking it. Bag all hardware in a zip-lock

## ROOM 8: ATTIC / STORAGE

*This covers any attic space, crawl space, basement storage, off-site storage unit, or the "back of the closet" overflow zone. If you don't have a formal attic, apply this to wherever your long-term storage lives.*

### Estimated Effort
| Metric | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Total boxes | 4–10 (highly variable — could be more if you've been storing for years) |
| Suggested box mix | 2–4 small, 2–4 medium, 2–4 large |
| Non-boxed items | Luggage, holiday trees, furniture pieces, bins |
| Time to declutter | 3–5 hours (this is the room people underestimate the most) |
| Time to pack | 2–3 hours (most of it is already in bins or boxes, just needs evaluation and relabeling) |
| Recommended schedule | Declutter in Week 6 or 7 — do this room FIRST. It's the easiest to forget and the hardest to rush. Pack keepers in Week 4. |

### The Attic Rule

**If it's been in your attic for more than 2 years and you forgot it existed, you don't need it.** The attic is where things go to be forgotten. Be honest with yourself. This room usually produces the highest volume of donations and trash.

### Declutter First

| Category | Keep | Sell / Donate | Trash |
|---|---|---|---|
| Holiday decorations | Your favorite tree, lights that work, ornaments with sentimental value, 1 box per holiday max | Duplicate or excess decorations, items from a "phase" (the year you went all-in on inflatables) | Broken lights (cut the plug off before trashing to prevent hazard), shattered ornaments, dried-out wreaths |
| Luggage and bags | 1 large suitcase per person, 1 carry-on per person, 1 duffel | Excess bags, broken-zippered luggage, old backpacks | Torn, broken-wheeled, musty luggage |
| Keepsakes and memorabilia | Items that genuinely make you feel something when you hold them. Photographs (always keep). Letters from people you love. | Participation trophies, dried corsages, ticket stubs you'll never look at again | Moldy, water-damaged, rodent-chewed items (photograph them before discarding if they're sentimental) |
| Old electronics | Nothing — if it's in the attic, you've already replaced it | Sell: working laptops, tablets, gaming consoles, cameras | Recycle: dead electronics at Best Buy, Staples, or a local e-waste center. Do not trash. |
| Baby / kid items | Only if relevant to your future plans | Donate to shelters, churches, or parents' groups | Recalled, broken, or stained beyond use |
| Old furniture | Only if it's quality and fits the new space | Sell or donate — this is the biggest space-saver in the truck | Broken, wobbly, particle board that won't survive the move |
| Boxes of "I'll sort this later" | Sort them now. That's the whole point. Apply the decision flow to every item. | — | — |
| Textbooks and old papers | Almost never worth keeping unless you're actively in the field | Sell textbooks on BookScouter.com or Amazon | Recycle outdated editions, old notebooks, printed coursework |
| Collections | Keep if you actively enjoy and display them | Sell valuable collections (coins, cards, vintage items) on eBay or specialty forums | Broken or incomplete sets with no value |

### The Photo Box Problem

Almost everyone has a box of unsorted photos in their attic. Here's the fastest approach:

1. **Don't try to sort them now.** You will lose an entire weekend.
2. Put the whole box in a medium moving box, label it 🟢 OPEN LATER.
3. Set a calendar reminder for 1 month after the move: "Sort the photo box."
4. Consider scanning them later with Google PhotoScan (free app) or a service like ScanMyPhotos.
5. **Photographs always make the move.** They are irreplaceable. Never throw out photos.

### Packing Order

**Pack in Week 4 (immediately after decluttering):**
- [ ] Holiday decorations — wrap fragile ornaments individually in tissue paper or packing paper, pack in small or medium boxes with dividers or egg-carton-style padding
- [ ] Keepsakes and memorabilia — small boxes, padded well
- [ ] Repack storage bins with only the items you're keeping, label with destination room and contents
- [ ] Luggage — don't waste space inside suitcases. Pack soft items inside them: off-season clothes, towels, stuffed animals, blankets. A suitcase full of towels rolls right onto the truck.

**Pack in Week 3:**
- [ ] Old furniture pieces — disassemble what you can. Bag all hardware (screws, bolts, cam locks) in a labeled zip-lock and tape it to the furniture piece.
- [ ] Remaining bins and boxes after re-evaluation
- [ ] Artificial holiday tree — fits back in the original box if you kept it. If not, wrap in a trash bag and tape closed.

**Pack last:**
- [ ] Nothing. The attic should be fully packed and cleared by Week 3. If anything is still up there in Week 2, you probably don't need it.
- [ ] **Do a final attic walk-through on move day.** It's the most forgotten space. Check every corner, shelf, and rafter. Bring a flashlight.

### Fragile Packing Tips — Attic Specific
- **Ornaments:** Wrap each one in tissue paper or packing paper. Use egg cartons, cupcake liners, or sock pairs as individual cushions. Pack in small boxes — ornaments are light but crush easily under weight.
- **Framed photos and art:** Tape an X across glass, wrap in bubble wrap, pack vertically (not flat) in a box with cardboard dividers between each frame.
- **Mirrors stored in attic:** Same treatment as framed art — X tape, bubble wrap, vertical packing. If the mirror is large, build a cardboard sandwich (two pieces of cardboard larger than the mirror, taped together around the wrapped mirror) or buy a mirror box from U-Haul (~$5–$15).
- **China, crystal, or heirloom dishes stored in attic:** Treat these like kitchen fragiles — wrap each piece individually, pack plates on edge, use small boxes, never stack heavy items on top.

### Box Labels for This Room
```
ATTIC — Holiday decorations, ornaments (fragile) — 🟢 OPEN LATER ⚠️ FRAGILE
ATTIC — Keepsakes, photos, memorabilia — 🟢 OPEN LATER
ATTIC — Stored bedding / off-season in suitcase — 🟢 OPEN LATER
ATTIC — [Contents of each re-evaluated bin] — 🟢 OPEN LATER
```

## ROOM 9: OUTDOOR GEAR

*This covers patio furniture, grill, camping gear, sports equipment, yard tools not already covered in the garage section, and anything stored on a deck, porch, or shed.*

### Estimated Effort
| Metric | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Total boxes | 2–5 (most outdoor gear is loose or in bags) |
| Suggested box mix | 1–2 small, 1–2 medium, 1 large |
| Non-boxed items | Patio furniture, grill, tent, camping chairs, cooler |
| Time to declutter | 1–2 hours |
| Time to pack | 1–2 hours |
| Recommended schedule | Declutter in Week 5. Pack in Week 3. Drain grill propane and prep large items in Week 2. |

### Declutter First

| Category | Keep | Sell / Donate | Trash |
|---|---|---|---|
| Patio furniture | Quality pieces that fit the new space (check: will you have a patio or yard in Oregon?) | Cheap or bulky items — sell on Marketplace. Patio furniture is easy to sell in spring/summer, harder in fall/winter. Time your listing. | Rusted, broken, sun-rotted, wobbly |
| Grill | **Decision point:** Charcoal grills are cheap to replace (~$30–$100 for a basic Weber). Gas grills are bulkier but more expensive. If yours is a quality gas grill, consider keeping it. If it's a $60 charcoal grill, sell it for $20 and buy a new one in Oregon. | Sell if not worth the truck space | Rusted-out, broken grates, non-functional ignition |
| Camping gear | Tent, sleeping bags, sleeping pads, camp stove, headlamps, cooler — keep if you camp | Gear you haven't used in 2+ years | Torn tents, broken poles, punctured pads, expired fuel canisters |
| Sports equipment | Equipment for sports you actively play | Old gear, outgrown items, "I'll get back into it" items you haven't touched in years | Broken, deflated beyond repair, cracked helmets |
| Garden hose and sprinklers | 1 good hose if you'll have a yard | Excess hoses, broken sprinkler heads | Cracked, kinked, leaking hoses |
| Outdoor toys or games | Cornhole, frisbees, etc. that you use | Broken or incomplete sets | — |
| Firewood | **Do not move firewood across state lines.** This is a real rule. Invasive insects (like emerald ash borer, which is present in Ohio) travel in firewood. Use it, give it to a neighbor, or leave it. | Give it away on Buy Nothing or Nextdoor | — |
| Pots and planters | 2–3 favorites that aren't too heavy | Cheap terracotta and plastic pots (heavy to move, cheap to replace) | Cracked, broken |

### Grill Prep
- **If keeping a gas grill:** Disconnect and properly dispose of the propane tank (see hazardous disposal section below). Remove grates, clean them, wrap them in an old towel or trash bag. Tape all loose parts. The grill body goes on the truck unwrapped or wrapped in stretch wrap.
- **If keeping a charcoal grill:** Empty all ash and charcoal. Clean the interior. Bag the grates. Tape the lid closed or wrap in stretch wrap.
- **Movers' rule:** Most movers will take a clean, empty, propane-free grill. Confirm with yours. They will not take propane tanks, lighter fluid, or charcoal.

### Camping Gear Packing Tips
- **Tent:** Clean and dry it completely before packing. A damp tent will mildew in transit. Roll it tightly and pack in its stuff sack. If the stuff sack is lost, use a trash bag cinched with a cord.
- **Sleeping bags:** Compress in stuff sacks or vacuum-seal bags. Don't store compressed for more than a few weeks — it damages insulation long-term. Unpack and loft them when you arrive.
- **Camp stove:** Disconnect and remove all fuel canisters. The stove itself can be packed. The fuel cannot go on a truck. Use it up, give it away, or dispose of it.
- **Cooler:** Clean it, dry it completely, leave it open to air out for a day. Then use it as packing space — fill it with soft items (towels, hats, gloves) or use it as your road-trip cooler on move day. Dual purpose.

### Packing Order

**Pack in Week 3:**
- [ ] Camping gear — tent, sleeping bags, pads, camp kitchen items
- [ ] Sports equipment — deflate balls slightly, bag small items, wrap rackets and bats in bubble wrap or towels
- [ ] Outdoor games
- [ ] Garden hose — drain completely, coil tightly, secure with a bungee or zip tie
- [ ] Small pots and planters — wrap terracotta in bubble wrap (or let them go)
- [ ] Outdoor decor, string lights, citronella candles

**Pack in Week 2:**
- [ ] Patio furniture — clean, fold what folds, stack what stacks, wrap legs in bubble wrap or towels to prevent scratching other items on the truck
- [ ] Grill — cleaned, emptied, propane-free, taped or wrapped
- [ ] Remaining yard tools not covered in the garage section

**Pack last:**
- [ ] Doormat — shake it out and toss it on the truck or in the car
- [ ] Any plants you're taking — water them the morning of, put them in the car (not the truck — temperature extremes will kill them). Note: Oregon has agricultural inspection rules. Most common houseplants are fine, but check the Oregon Department of Agriculture guidelines if you're bringing outdoor plants, soil, or anything unusual. A quick search before you go can avoid a problem at the border or down the road.
- [ ] Porch or patio lights if you own them (not if they're the landlord's)

OUTDOOR — Sports equipment — 🟢 OPEN LATER
OUTDOOR — Garden hose, tools, planters — 🟢 OPEN LATER
OUTDOOR — Outdoor games, decor, lights — 🟢 OPEN LATER

## PRINTABLE BOX LABEL TEMPLATE

Sized for **Avery 5164** (3⅓″ × 4″, 6 per sheet) or **Avery 5163** (2″ × 4″, 10 per sheet). The layout below works for either — just adjust font size. If you don't have label sheets, you can print on regular paper and tape them to boxes, or just copy the format by hand with a Sharpie.

### Template Layout (one label)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                             │
│  ROOM: ____________________________________│
│                                             │
│  CONTENTS: ________________________________│
│                                             │
│  _________________________________________  │
│                                             │
│  PRIORITY:  🔴 OPEN FIRST                  │
│             🟡 OPEN SOON                   │
│             🟢 OPEN LATER                  │
│             (circle one)                    │
│                                             │
│  ⚠️  FRAGILE?   YES  /  NO                 │
│                                             │
│  BOX ___ OF ___    THIS SIDE UP  ↑         │
│                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### How to Print

**Option A — Handwritten (fastest):**
Print 60–80 blank copies of the template above on regular paper, 2 per page. Cut them out. Fill in by hand with a Sharpie as you pack each box. Tape to two sides of the box.

**Option B — Avery labels (cleanest):**
1. Go to **avery.com/templates**
2. Select product **5164** (6 per sheet, 3⅓″ × 4″)
3. Use their free Design & Print tool
4. Create a label with this layout:

```

## FREE BOXES IN OHIO — WHERE, WHEN, AND HOW

### Best Chain Sources

| Store | What to Ask For | Best Time to Ask | Quality | Tips |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Liquor stores (state-run or independent)** | Liquor boxes with dividers | Anytime — they always have them | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Thick cardboard, built-in dividers perfect for glasses and bottles | Best free boxes available. Dividers double as dish and glass separators. Ask for cases that held wine or spirits (thicker cardboard than beer boxes). |
| **Grocery stores (Kroger, Aldi, Giant Eagle)** | Banana boxes, apple boxes, egg boxes | Early morning, right after stocking (5–8 AM or ask the night crew) | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ Banana boxes have lids and handles, very sturdy | Banana boxes are the gold standard of free boxes. They have built-in handles and lids. Ask the produce department specifically. Go early — they break them down fast. |
| **Costco / Sam's Club** | Any display boxes from the floor | During restocking (early morning or ask a manager) | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ Large, thick, designed to hold heavy product | Apple boxes and diaper boxes are especially good. Avoid produce boxes that held wet items (they'll be soft or damp). |
| **Walmart** | Shipping boxes from the back | Ask a stocking associate during the overnight or early morning shift | ⭐⭐⭐ Varies widely in size and quality | Hit or miss. Some stores will save them if you ask nicely a day ahead. |
| **Target** | Shipping boxes from the back | Same as Walmart — early morning | ⭐⭐⭐ Similar to Walmart | Ask Guest Services to check with the back room team. |
| **Home Depot / Lowe's** | Appliance boxes (huge), tile boxes (small and very strong) | Anytime — ask at the customer service desk | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ Appliance boxes are great for large items, tile boxes are nearly indestructible for heavy items | Appliance boxes are great for lampshades, pillows, and bulky light items. |
| **Bookstores (Half Price Books, Barnes & Noble, local shops)** | Book shipping boxes | Anytime | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Small, thick, perfect for heavy items like tools and books | Book boxes are the perfect size for heavy loads. They're small so you won't over-pack them. |
| **McDonald's / Starbucks / fast food** | Fry boxes, supply boxes | Ask a manager during a slow period | ⭐⭐ Smaller, grease risk | Only use clean, dry ones. Good for lightweight items. |
| **U-Haul Customer Connect / Box Exchange** | Used moving boxes left by other customers | Check the U-Haul location near you — many have a free box shelf or online listing | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ Already sized for moving | Also check uhaul.com/exchange for local free box listings. |

### Online Free Box Sources

| Source | How | Tips |
|---|---|---|
| **Facebook Marketplace** | Search "free moving boxes" in your area | People post free boxes constantly right after they move in. Set an alert for the search term. |
| **Buy Nothing Group** (Facebook) | Post an ISO (in search of) for moving boxes | These groups are hyperlocal and very responsive. Post early in the week. |
| **Nextdoor** | Post a request or search "boxes" | Neighbors love to get rid of boxes. |
| **Craigslist Free section** | Search "moving boxes" under Free | Check daily — they go fast. |
| **Freecycle.org** | Post a Wanted listing | Slower than Facebook but still active in many Ohio cities. |

### Timing Tips

- **Best days to get store boxes:** Tuesday through Thursday mornings. Monday is restocking after the weekend, but boxes are often already broken down. By Friday, the week's boxes are gone.
- **Best time of day:** 6–9 AM, right after the overnight or early morning stocking shift.
- **Call ahead.** Call the store the day before and ask them to set aside boxes for you. Say: *"I'm moving and would love any clean, sturdy boxes you're breaking down. Can I pick some up tomorrow morning?"* Most stores will say yes.
- **Bring your own bags or car space.** Boxes are bulky — bring a vehicle that can handle them, or flatten them and re-tape at home.
- **Go twice.** One trip probably won't get you everything. Plan two trips, a few days apart, to different stores.
- **Inspect before loading.** Reject any box that is damp, stained, torn, or smells like food. A weak box will fail when you're carrying dishes.

## HAZARDOUS ITEMS — SPECIAL DISPOSAL REQUIRED

**These items cannot go on a moving truck (professional or DIY rental). Most are also illegal to put in regular trash.** Schedule disposal before move day.

### Disposal Checklist

| Item | Where Found | How to Dispose | Where in Ohio | Lead Time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Propane tanks** (grill-size 20 lb) | Garage, patio | Exchange at a Blue Rhino or AmeriGas location (Home Depot, Walmart, gas stations) for a store credit or new tank. Or take to a local hazardous waste collection. Do NOT put in trash. | Blue Rhino locations statewide; check your county's solid waste district for HHW events | Same day at exchange locations |
| **Small propane canisters** (1 lb, camping) | Garage, camping gear | If completely empty, puncture with a can opener and recycle as metal. If not empty, take to hazardous waste collection. Some areas accept them at scrap metal recyclers. | County HHW events or facilities | Check schedule — HHW events often run monthly or quarterly |
| **Gasoline** | Garage, lawn mower, gas cans | Use it up in your mower or car. If you can't, take it to a hazardous waste facility. Never pour it down a drain or put it in trash. | County HHW facility | Same day at permanent facilities |
| **Motor oil and filters** | Garage | Take to any auto parts store (AutoZone, O'Reilly, Advance Auto Parts) — they accept used oil for free by law in Ohio. | Any auto parts store | Same day, walk in |
| **Paint (latex)** | Garage, attic | If less than ¼ full: open the can, mix in cat litter or sawdust, let it dry solid, then put the dried can in regular trash. If usable: donate to Habitat ReStore. | Habitat ReStore for usable paint. Trash for dried-out cans. HHW for large quantities. | 1–2 days drying time for the cat litter method |
| **Paint (oil-based, stains, varnishes)** | Garage, attic | These are hazardous waste. Do not put in trash. Take to a county HHW event or facility. | County HHW facility | Check schedule |
| **Cleaning solvents and chemicals** (turpentine, paint thinner, mineral spirits, pool chemicals) | Garage, under sinks | Hazardous waste. Take to county HHW. | County HHW facility | Check schedule |
| **Pesticides and herbicides** | Garage, shed | Hazardous waste. Take to county HHW. | County HHW facility | Check schedule |
| **Batteries — alkaline (AA, AAA, C, D, 9V)** | Everywhere | In Ohio, standard alkaline batteries can go in regular trash. However, Best Buy, Batteries Plus, and Home Depot accept them for recycling if you prefer. | Trash or any of those retailers | Same day |
| **Batteries — lithium, rechargeable, button cell** | Electronics, tools, remotes, hearing aids | Do NOT put these in trash — fire risk. Take to Best Buy, Batteries Plus, Home Depot, or Staples for free recycling. | Best Buy, Batteries Plus, Staples, Home Depot | Same day, walk in |
| **Car batteries** | Garage, car | Take to any auto parts store — they accept them for free and may give you a core credit ($5–$15). | AutoZone, O'Reilly, Advance Auto Parts | Same day |
| **Electronics (old computers, TVs, monitors, phones)** | Attic, office, garage | Do not trash. Take to Best Buy (free recycling for most items, limit 3 per household per day) or a local e-waste recycler. Wipe hard drives first
